text: Refinements of D-0249 from #369's second review. The factory merges a watched draft only at the head whose gate, scope, lock and trusted files it checked: it reads the pull request again after marking it ready, takes no step if the head moved, and pins the merge to the checked head, so a push while it marks the draft ready waits for CI on it. When a build that passed finds a draft open from its branch and GitHub refuses to mark it ready, the build's post is a failure that names the draft, FailUnready, which the protocol counts as a build that left a draft and a writer's retry watches again. An error GitHub may not repeat, such as a 502, is tried again on the next poll rather than taken as a refusal, there and wherever the factory takes GitHub's answer as one. A draft no retry watched gets one post, FailDraft, which the protocol counts as one the factory can't merge, and the issue leaves the pull request's state, so the factory hears commands again, where before it refused and relabeled the issue every poll. A draft counts as watched when the factory answered a retry of it, whether or not the retry is still there. While GitHub hasn't said whether it can merge a watched draft, the factory says so once in its log.
